title: Mold Inspection in Glendale, CA
metaDescription: Independent mold inspection in Glendale, CA with thermal imaging and moisture meters. Non-invasive, from $295. Call ACD Mold at (424) 352-7039.
intro: ACD Mold is an independent mold inspection and testing company serving Glendale and the surrounding Verdugo foothills. An inspector travels to your home or building, maps moisture with thermal imaging and meters, and gives you a clear read on whether you have a mold problem, where the water is coming from, and what (if anything) needs to happen next. We diagnose and verify work; we do not perform the removal ourselves, which keeps our assessment free of any incentive to over-recommend. Call (424) 352-7039 to schedule.

sections.heading: What a mold inspection covers in Glendale
paragraphs: A mold inspection is a structured visual and moisture assessment of the areas you are concerned about. The goal is to confirm whether active moisture or mold growth is present, trace it back to its source, and document the finding so you can make a decision. Glendale homes range from century-old hillside houses in Verdugo Woodlands to downtown condo towers, so the inspection is shaped around the building in front of us rather than a fixed checklist. A typical visit covers the reported problem area, adjacent assemblies, and any accessible attic, crawlspace, or under-sink cabinetry, looking for the conditions that let mold grow: standing water, chronic dampness, condensation, and poor drainage or ventilation. Laboratory testing can be added where useful, but it is an option rather than a default.
list: Visual assessment of the areas of concern and adjacent assemblies
Thermal imaging to find temperature differentials that often mark hidden moisture
Moisture-meter readings on walls, ceilings, subfloors, and cabinetry
A review of the likely moisture source so the underlying cause can be fixed
A plain-language summary of findings and recommended next steps

sections.heading: Why Glendale's foothills and housing stock matter
paragraphs: Glendale sits against the Verdugo Mountains and San Rafael Hills, and that geography drives many of the moisture issues we are asked to look at. Hillside Spanish-revival homes in neighborhoods like Adams Hill and Verdugo Woodlands sit on slopes where water moves downhill through soil and can seep against foundations and lower-level walls, especially after a wet winter. Many of these older homes also retain portions of their original plumbing, which can leak slowly before anyone notices a stain.

Elsewhere the pattern changes: mid-century duplexes often have low-slope roofs and aging supply lines, while the downtown high-rise condos commonly see HVAC-related condensation at air handlers and ductwork. None of this is proprietary data on our part; it is the well-known building physics of a foothill city with a wide mix of housing eras. The practical point is that the smartest place to put the moisture meter differs between a 1925 hillside bungalow and a 2008 condo, and the inspection adapts accordingly.

sections.heading: What to expect at the appointment
paragraphs: The inspector arrives at the scheduled time, confirms what prompted the call, and asks a few questions about the history of any leaks, past water damage, or recent repairs. That context matters, because a stain from a roof leak that was fixed three years ago calls for a very different conclusion than a baseboard that is wet today.

The moisture survey itself is non-invasive. Thermal cameras and moisture meters read temperature and moisture differentials at the surface; it is worth being clear that these instruments do not see mold through walls and cannot by themselves confirm what is behind a finished surface. They point us to the areas worth a closer look. If a reading strongly suggests a concealed problem, we will discuss whether a small inspection opening or follow-up testing makes sense before anyone starts cutting into walls. Most residential visits take roughly one to two hours depending on the size of the home and how many areas are involved.

sections.heading: Honest pricing and timing
paragraphs: A standard thermal-and-moisture inspection runs $295 to $595, with the range driven mainly by the size of the property and how many separate areas need to be assessed. A single condo or a focused one-room concern sits at the lower end; a larger multi-level hillside home with an attic and crawlspace sits higher.

Laboratory testing, when you choose to add it, is priced separately: roughly $95 per surface sample or $145 to $195 per air sample, plus the accredited-lab analysis. You will know which samples are being recommended, and why, before anything is collected. We can usually schedule an inspection within a few days, and you receive a written summary of findings after the visit; when samples are sent to the lab, results typically follow within a few business days.

sections.heading: When testing helps and when it does not
paragraphs: Testing is genuinely useful in some situations and unnecessary in others, and we try to be straight about which is which. The U.S. EPA notes that when mold is already visible, sampling is usually not needed, because the conclusion is the same either way: the mold should be removed and the moisture source corrected. The California Department of Public Health recommends promptly removing all visible mold regardless of area, without routine measuring, since there are no health-based spore thresholds to measure against.

Testing earns its keep when the question is not yet answered: a musty odor with no visible source, air you want checked in a space with no growth, or an indoor-versus-outdoor baseline comparison. A sample characterizes what was in the air or on a surface at that spot and time; it does not diagnose illness or certify that a building is safe. On the DIY question, EPA offers a rough guide that a patch smaller than about ten square feet can often be cleaned by a homeowner taking sensible precautions, but that figure is EPA's practical cleanup guidance, not a California rule or a legal trigger.

People often call specifically about "black mold." Keeping it factual: per the CDC, "black mold" is not a distinct medical diagnosis, and a causal link between Stachybotrys and serious illness in otherwise-healthy people has not been established. Still, any indoor mold should be removed regardless of species, and people with asthma, mold allergies, or weakened immune systems may react more strongly. The right response depends on finding the moisture and addressing the growth, not on identifying a scary-sounding species.

sections.heading: How removal and clearance work
paragraphs: If the inspection finds mold that needs professional removal, ACD does not perform the physical remediation, and that separation is deliberate. The party diagnosing the problem and verifying the result is not the party paid to remove it, which removes the built-in conflict of interest that exists when one company both finds the mold and sells the demolition.

When removal is warranted, we can coordinate licensed, insured remediation partner crews, or you are welcome to use your own contractor. California has no state mold-specific license; remediation is carried out under a CSLB contractor license (commonly a B or C-61/D-64 classification) held by the crew doing the work. Once removal is complete, ACD can return to perform independent post-remediation clearance: confirming there is no remaining visible growth and, where appropriate, that indoor spore counts are at or below the outdoor baseline. That is the honest definition of a passing clearance, and because we were not paid to do the removal, our sign-off means what it says.

faqs.q: Do I need a mold test, or just an inspection?
faqs.a: Often just an inspection. EPA notes that when mold is already visible, sampling is usually unnecessary because the response is the same either way: remove the mold and fix the moisture. Testing helps mainly when there is no visible growth but you suspect a hidden source, or when you want an indoor-versus-outdoor baseline. We recommend samples only when they will answer a real question.

faqs.q: Can your thermal camera see mold inside my walls?
faqs.a: No. Thermal cameras and moisture meters detect temperature and moisture differentials at the surface; they do not see mold through walls. They point us toward concealed dampness worth a closer look, but confirming what is behind a finished surface may require a small inspection opening or follow-up testing, which we discuss with you first.

faqs.q: How much does a mold inspection in Glendale cost?
faqs.a: A standard thermal-and-moisture inspection is $295 to $595, depending mainly on the property's size and the number of areas assessed. Optional lab testing is about $95 per surface sample or $145 to $195 per air sample, plus accredited-lab analysis. You will know which samples are recommended, and why, before any are collected.

faqs.q: Do you remove the mold you find?
faqs.a: No, and that is intentional. ACD performs inspection, testing, and independent clearance only. If removal is needed, we can coordinate licensed, insured remediation partner crews, or you can use your own contractor. Keeping the company that diagnoses separate from the one that removes means our assessment and final clearance are not influenced by selling demolition work.

faqs.q: Why does Glendale seem to have moisture issues?
faqs.a: Largely the foothill geography and the mix of housing eras. Homes on the Verdugo slopes can see water move downhill against foundations after wet winters, and older hillside houses may have original plumbing that leaks slowly; mid-century duplexes and downtown HVAC condensation add their own patterns. These are general realities of the area, not a claim about any one address.

faqs.q: What does it mean to pass a post-remediation clearance?
faqs.a: After removal, clearance means no remaining visible mold growth and, where air sampling is used, indoor spore counts at or below the outdoor baseline. It does not certify a building permanently safe or diagnose anyone's health; it verifies that, at that time, the cleanup met the standard. Because ACD is not paid to do the removal, our clearance is independent of the crew's work.
